blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the accounting equation stops being a reconciliation check and becomes a lens for understanding the whole company. Assets represent everything the business uses to create value. Liabilities represent everything it has financed by borrowing, paying later, or deferring obligations. Equity represents what the owners have actually put in and earned over time.

The shape of the equation reveals strategy. A company with a large asset base and thin equity is leaning heavily on debt — comfortable in good times, precarious in bad. A company with growing equity and shrinking liabilities is compounding quietly, on its own strength. A company where receivables and inventory dominate the asset side may be working hard for customers who are slow to pay.

What matters at this level is not the equation itself, but the ability to read it as a story — and to ask the questions that story suggests before the numbers stop flattering them.

items.q: According to the text, what does the accounting equation become at senior level?
options: A lens for understanding the whole company
items.why: "the accounting equation stops being a reconciliation check and becomes a lens for understanding the whole company."

items.q: What does a large asset base combined with thin equity indicate?
options: The company has no liabilities to speak of
The company is leaning heavily on debt
The company is compounding on its own strength
items.why: "A company with a large asset base and thin equity is leaning heavily on debt."

items.q: A firm where receivables and inventory dominate the asset side suggests that…
options: it may be serving customers who are slow to pay
items.why: "receivables and inventory dominate the asset side may be working hard for customers who are slow to pay."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A healthy balance sheet in good times can turn precarious in bad ones.
The equation is most useful as a mechanical check that both sides tie out.
Reading the balance sheet is a matter of interpretation, not arithmetic.
The same equation can conceal very different strategies.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta justamente que, no nível sênior, o valor está na leitura estratégica — não em conferir se os dois lados batem.

items.q: What does "before the numbers stop flattering them" most strongly imply?
options: Balance sheets can look reassuring right up until a problem surfaces
Equity is the only figure worth trusting
items.why: Inferência: a aparência favorável não dura — a hora de perguntar é enquanto os números ainda tranquilizam.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry conduzindo o novo CFO pelos balanços de três concorrentes. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, here are three competitors, side by side. On the P&L they look almost indistinguishable — similar revenue, similar margins. It's only on the balance sheet that the strategies pull apart.

Take the first one. Enormous asset base, wafer-thin equity. Nearly everything is financed by debt and deferred obligations. In a strong year that flatters the returns beautifully. But the moment demand softens, that same leverage works against them — and there is very little equity underneath to absorb the shock.

Now compare the second. Equity has been climbing year after year, liabilities are shrinking, and no one outside is talking about it. That's a company compounding quietly, on its own strength. Unglamorous, but I'd back it in a downturn every time.

The third is the one I'd watch most closely. Receivables and inventory dominate the asset side. On paper the business is growing, but read the shape and you can see it's working hard for customers who are slow to pay. So my question to you is not which one earns the most this year — it's which one you'd still want to own when the numbers stop flattering them.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why do the three competitors look almost indistinguishable at first?
options: They report on the same balance sheet date
On the P&L they show similar revenue and margins
They operate in the same city
items.why: "On the P&L they look almost indistinguishable — similar revenue, similar margins."

items.q: What is Harry's concern about the FIRST company?
options: It refuses to take on any debt
There is little equity to absorb a downturn
It has too much idle cash
items.why: "very little equity underneath to absorb the shock" quando a demanda cai.

items.q: Why would Harry back the SECOND company in a downturn?
options: It carries the highest leverage of the three
It has the most exciting story in the market
It is growing equity and shrinking liabilities on its own strength
items.why: "Equity has been climbing… liabilities are shrinking… compounding quietly, on its own strength."

items.q: What does Harry imply about the THIRD company's growth?
options: Its growth may be tied up in customers who pay slowly
It is the safest bet of the three
items.why: Inferência: crescimento 'no papel', mas com recebíveis e estoque dominando — o dinheiro está preso em quem paga devagar.

items.q: What is the real question Harry puts to the CFO at the end?
options: Which company has the largest asset base
Which company has the newest management team
Which company earns the most this year
Which company you'd still want to own once the numbers stop flattering them
items.why: Inferência: ele desloca o critério do lucro do ano para a resiliência — quem você ainda quereria ter quando a aparência favorável acabar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Read the equation as a lens, not a checklist." Here, a lens is…
options: a way of seeing and interpreting
items.why: Lens = lente: um enquadramento pelo qual se enxerga e interpreta a empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When equity keeps climbing and debt keeps falling, the business is ___ quietly, without any outside noise."
items.why: To compound = compor-se, crescer sobre si mesmo — o retrato da segunda empresa.

items.q: "A deferred obligation sits on the balance sheet as…"
options: an asset available for immediate use
a gain the owners have earned
an amount the company must settle later
a cost already paid in full
items.why: Deferred obligation = obrigação diferida: algo devido que será liquidado mais adiante.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Receivables and inventory ___ the asset side, so most of the value is tied up rather than in cash."
items.why: To dominate = dominar: os dois itens ocupam a maior parte dos ativos.

items.q: "In a strong year, leverage can flatter the returns." To flatter here means to…
options: make them look better than they are
items.why: To flatter = favorecer/enfeitar: fazer os números parecerem melhores do que a realidade sustenta.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre balanço e estratégia. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the refinancing before we cut the debt." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "On paper the growth looks strong, but it doesn't stack up once you factor in slow-paying customers." To stack up means to…
items.why: To stack up = fazer sentido/sustentar-se quando examinado de perto.

items.q: "Too much of the balance sheet is tied up in inventory and receivables." Capital that is tied up is…
items.why: Tied up = preso/comprometido: o capital existe, mas não está disponível como caixa.

items.q: "None of these cosmetic adjustments will move the needle on solvency." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível — aqui, o contrário.

items.q: "When demand softened, the leverage caught up with them." This means the leverage…
options: eventually produced the consequences they had put off
items.why: Catch up with = alcançar: as consequências adiadas do endividamento acabam cobrando seu preço.
